'''Ronald Fuchs''' (January 27, 1932 – November 10, 2012) was an American theoretical physicist and professor at [[Iowa State University]]. He is recognized for his work on electromagnetic properties of solids, light scattering of small particles and nonlocal optical phenomena.

== Biography ==

Ernest Ronald Fuchs was born in Los Angeles, California in 1932, only child of Swiss-born Ernest Fuchs and Hanna Berta (Herren) Fuchs.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Ernest Ronald Fuchs Obituary, January 27, 1932 – November 10, 2012 |url=https://www.grandonfuneralandcremationcare.com/obituary/96120/Ernest-Ronald-Fuchs-of-Ames-Iowa/ |access-date=2022-12-13 |website=Ames, Iowa Funeral Home {{!}} Grandon Funeral and Cremation Care |language=en-US}}</ref>

Fuchs graduated from [[John Muir College]], [[Pasadena, California]] in 1950, and attended [[California Institute of Technology]] (Caltech) on a full scholarship. He graduated as top in his class with a B.S. in physics in 1954. He then pursued graduate studies in physics at the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]], where he earned his M.S. in 1955 and his PhD in 1957.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0">{{cite journal |title=Obituary of Ronald Fuchs (1932-2012) |journal=Physics Today |date=7 June 2013 |doi=10.1063/PT.4.2579 }}</ref> His PhD thesis focused on the absorption of light of [[alkali metal halide]]s, under the supervision of [[Frederick Seitz]].<ref>{{cite thesis |last1=Fuchs |first1=Ronald |title=The Autoionization of The Beta Center and The Fine Structure of The Beta-Band in Sodium-Chloride |date=1957 |hdl=2142/76306 }}{{psc|date=February 2024}}</ref>

After completing his doctoral studies, Fuchs worked as a [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright Scholar]] with a National Science Foundation Fellowship at the [[University of Stuttgart]], Germany, and later worked at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) Laboratory for Insulation Research from 1958 to 1961.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

In 1961, Fuchs joined the faculty of the Iowa State University's department of physics and astronomy as an assistant professor. He was promoted to full professorship in 1974 and became [[emeritus]] in 1996.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" />

In 1969, he became a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=APS Fellow Archive |url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm |access-date=2022-12-14 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref>

Throughout his career, Fuchs arranged two-year-long faculty leave as visiting professor to Germany. The first was to the [[Max Planck Institute for Solid State Research]] from 1973 to 1974, and the second was to the [[Freie Universitaet Berlin]] and the [[Fritz Haber Institute of the Max Planck Society]] from 1986 to 1987. He also took a year-long Overseas Fellowship at the [[Cavendish Laboratory]] at the [[University of Cambridge]] in the United Kingdom from 1996 to 1997.<ref name=":1" />

He died in a house in [[Ames, Iowa]], as a consequence of a [[plasmacytoma]].<ref name=":1" />

== Research ==
Fuchs worked on the theory of the optical properties and non-local effects of metals and insulators, including [[thin film]]s, small particles, rough surfaces, and disordered systems. He also worked on surface reflectance spectroscopy and [[electron energy loss spectroscopy]] of inhomogeneous systems.<ref name=":2" />

The theory of [[Kliewer–Fuchs mode]]s, related to vibrational modes found on the surface of [[Insulator (electricity)|insulating crystals]], was developed by Fuchs and [[Kenneth Lee Kliewer]] in 1965.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite book |last=Mahan |first=Gerald D. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v3FVOH2XK4gC&q=kenneth+kliewer+ronald+fuchs |title=Condensed Matter in a Nutshell |date=2011 |publisher=Princeton University Press |isbn=978-0-691-14016-2 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Fuchs |first1=Ronald |last2=Kliewer |first2=K. L. |title=Optical Modes of Vibration in an Ionic Crystal Slab |journal=Physical Review |date=13 December 1965 |volume=140 |issue=6A |pages=A2076–A2088 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.140.A2076 }}{{psc|date=February 2024}}</ref> Fuchs developed the theory of surface modes in [[ionic crystal]] cubes exposed to a uniform electric fields.<ref name=":12">{{Cite web |title=Ernest Ronald Fuchs Obituary, January 27, 1932 – November 10, 2012 |url=https://www.grandonfuneralandcremationcare.com/obituary/96120/Ernest-Ronald-Fuchs-of-Ames-Iowa/ |access-date=2022-12-13 |website=Ames, Iowa Funeral Home {{!}} Grandon Funeral and Cremation Care |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Fuchs |first1=R. |title=Theory of the optical properties of ionic crystal cubes |journal=Physical Review B |date=15 February 1975 |volume=11 |issue=4 |pages=1732–1740 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.11.1732 }}{{psc|date=February 2024}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
* For his 75th birthday, a conference was held in [[Puebla (city)|Puebla, Mexico]] in 2007 to honor Fuchs "in recognition for his contributions to nonlocal optics and optical properties of small particles and his fruitful collaborations with Latin American physicists".<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Barrera |first=Rubén G. |date=2006 |title=A Portrait of Ronald Fuchs on his 75th Birthday |url=https://www.fisica.unam.mx/personales/rbarrera/pdf/ps/ron-fuchs-06.pdf |website=Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México UNAM}}</ref>
*He was given the [[American Physical Society]] recognition for Outstanding Referees in 2009.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Physical Review Journals – Outstanding Referees |url=https://journals.aps.org/OutstandingReferees |access-date=2022-12-13 |website=journals.aps.org}}</ref>
